name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
description: Narrow elevated ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Features exceptional long-duration solar illumination during the southern lunar summer with rapid access to cryogenic permanently shadowed volatile traps.
scientific_value: Direct access to Shackleton crater cold traps where surface and subsurface water ice volatiles are predicted. Pristine South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin impact melt sampling.

name: Malapert Mountain (Alpha)
description: Prominent highland massif rising ~5 km above surrounding topography. Offers nearly continuous direct line-of-sight to Earth, making it the premier South Pole site for high-bandwidth direct-to-Earth communications.
scientific_value: Highland crustal stratigraphy, deep crustal lunar samples from ancient pre-Nectarian impacts, and long-baseline astronomical observation staging.

name: Nobile Crater Rim 1
description: Broad rolling plateau along the western rim of Nobile crater. Chosen as the primary landing environment for NASA's VIPER rover due to navigable slopes and proximity to volatile concentration zones.
scientific_value: Ground-truth correlation of orbital neutron spectroscopy volatile signatures, regolith mechanics, and micro-cold-trap temperature profiling.

name: Haworth Crater Rim
description: High relief rim section bordering Haworth crater. Immediate proximity to one of the coldest permanently shadowed craters in the south polar cluster (< 40 Kelvin).
scientific_value: Ultra-cold volatile condensation profiling (carbon monoxide, methane, and complex organics trapped alongside water ice).

name: Faustini Crater Rim A
description: Bench-like elevated terrain along the north-western rim of Faustini crater. Moderate slopes provide accessible rover descent paths into shaded terrain.
scientific_value: Volatile migration mechanisms, regolith maturity gradients between sunlit rim and crater floor shadowed frost deposits.

name: Peak Near Amundsen Rim
description: Elevated topographical peak adjacent to Amundsen crater. Extremely benign slopes (< 5 degrees) across a wide landing corridor with favorable Earth contact.
scientific_value: Central peak impact melt rocks, age dating of the Amundsen impact event, and calibration of the lunar impact chronology curve.

name: de Gerlache Crater Rim 2
description: Crest of the de Gerlache crater rim. High solar availability with steep local escarpments that require precision hazard avoidance during descent.
scientific_value: Structural deformation of crater walls, space weathering rates under grazing solar incidence angles.

name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
description: Extensive high-altitude plateau providing one of the flattest terrain profiles in the lunar south polar region. Exceptional clearance for heavy cargo landers.
scientific_value: Deep South Pole-Aitken basin ejecta stratigraphy and potential anorthositic ancient lunar crust samples.
